text: Two things about that site before we leave it, because a leaderboard is an easy thing to misread.

First. Read the price and the speed columns alongside the intelligence one, not after it. A model two points down the index at a third of the cost is very often the correct choice, and if you only ever look at the top row you will never once find it.

Second, and this is the one that catches people out. A benchmark measures the model. It does not measure the model plus your tools, plus your agents file, plus your workflow. And what you actually ship is the whole of that.

Which is why a middling model in a well set up environment routinely beats the top of the leaderboard in a badly set up one. The last three lectures were about the parts of that stack you control. This chart is the one part you do not.
So read it the way you would read a spec sheet for a component. It tells you what is possible. It does not tell you what you will build.
